title: Charred Tomatillo Salsa Verde
summary: Tomatillos, onion, chillies and garlic blistered in a hot pan, pulsed to a chunky salsa and finished with coriander, lime and salt.

ingredients.note: seed them for a milder salsa

ingredients.item: fresh coriander, leaves and tender stems
lime juice, plus wedges to serve
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Blister the vegetables
steps.text: Heat the oil in the heavy pan over medium-high heat. Lay in the tomatillos cut-side down with the onion wedges, chillies and garlic. Cook for 8-10 min, turning occasionally, until blackened in patches and the tomatillos slump and release juice. Lift the garlic out once golden, after about 3 min, so it does not turn bitter.

steps.title: Let it cool
steps.text: Tip the vegetables and every bit of juice onto a plate and leave for 10 min, so the salsa keeps its fresh colour and is safe to blend.

steps.title: Pulse roughly
steps.text: Put the vegetables in the processor with half the coriander and pulse in short bursts to a chunky purée. Stop while you can still see pieces of tomatillo and onion.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Finely chop the rest of the coriander and stir it in with the lime juice and salt. Taste and add more lime or salt as needed; it should be tart, bright and gently hot.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon into a bowl and serve with tortilla chips and lime wedges, or spoon it over tacos, fried eggs or grilled chicken.

tips: Choose firm, bright green tomatillos that fill their husks; rinse off the sticky coating after husking.
Taste a sliver of each chilli first, as heat varies widely.
Char one extra chilli whole to serve alongside, as in the photo.
The salsa thickens as it chills; loosen with a spoonful of water if needed.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 4 days. Freeze for up to 2 months; stir well after thawing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
